item.title: Subject: Preload appears to repeatedly delete cache files – WooCommerce site
item.dc:creator: potatodesign
item.description:
Replies: 2

Subject: Preload appears to repeatedly delete cache files – WooCommerce site

Hi,

I’m using WP Super Cache on my WooCommerce website, https://jadaneida.no/, hosted by Domeneshop in Norway.

I’m trying to improve loading times, particularly on mobile devices. The site uses WordPress, Divi 5 and WooCommerce, with approximately 106 published products.

Current configuration:

  • Cache enabled
  • Expert delivery method
  • Compression enabled
  • Cache Rebuild enabled
  • Caching disabled for logged-in users
  • Preload refresh interval: 0 minutes (currently disabled)
  • Preload all posts enabled
  • Preload mode enabled (garbage collection disabled)
  • Preload categories and taxonomies enabled

The problem

When I previously ran Preload, it appeared to build cache files, but the number of cached pages subsequently decreased.

The debug log also showed repeated deletion of cache files during the preload process.

For example:

wp_cron_preload_cache: scheduling the next preload in 3 seconds

wpsc_delete_files: deleting .../wp-content/cache/supercache/jadaneida.no/

wpsc_delete_files: deleting index-https.html.gz
wpsc_delete_files: deleting index-https.html

Similar entries appeared repeatedly during the preload process.

I understand that these particular log entries concern the homepage cache directory, so they do not necessarily mean that all product caches were deleted.

Some product pages were cached successfully, while others showed messages such as:

DONOTCACHEPAGE defined. Caching disabled.

What I’ve checked

  • The WP Super Cache cache test passes successfully, with matching timestamps.
  • Expert caching appears to work normally.
  • WP Crontrol currently shows no scheduled preload events.
  • The cache statistics currently show 64 cached pages.
  • Preload is currently disabled, with the refresh interval set to 0.

My questions

  1. Is it normal for the preload process to repeatedly delete the homepage cache files?
  2. Could this behaviour explain why the number of cached pages decreases after preloading?
  3. Is there a recommended preload configuration for a WooCommerce website with around 100 products?
  4. What could cause DONOTCACHEPAGE to be defined on some product pages during preloading?
  5. Would you recommend scheduled preloading or a different approach to ensure that product pages are cached before customers visit them?

My main concern is that visitors should not have to wait for WordPress, WooCommerce and Divi to generate a page on their first visit.

I’d appreciate any advice on configuring WP Super Cache reliably for this type of website.

Thanks in advance!

item.title: WP Super Cache 3.1.4 – Caches unexpectedly cleared
item.dc:creator: Sacha
item.description:
Replies: 7

Hello,
I’m experiencing a recurring issue with WP Super Cache 3.1.4 on my WordPress website.

My website contains approximately 2,200 pages, and I use the preload feature to keep the site cached and improve performance.

The problem is that both WP-Cache and SuperCache occasionally get completely cleared, with their respective counters suddenly dropping to zero.

This is particularly frustrating because rebuilding the cache takes considerable time and appears to negatively affect website performance during the process.

I’ve noticed that activating a WordPress plugin can trigger this behavior, even when the plugin itself has no obvious connection to caching.

For example, the most recent incident occurred immediately after activating Query Monitor. Both cache counters dropped to zero, and the cache had to be rebuilt.

However, I don’t believe this issue is necessarily specific to Query Monitor. I’m more concerned about the possibility that activating or updating plugins, or certain WordPress events, might trigger an unexpected full-cache purge.

My current configuration:

  • WP Super Cache 3.1.4
  • Preloading enabled
  • Cache timeout: 86,400 seconds
  • Garbage collection interval: 3,600 seconds
  • The option to clear all cached files when a post is published or updated is disabled
  • WordPress hosted by Infomaniak

I’ve also enabled WP Super Cache debugging. During the latest incident, the log recorded the plugin activation and a prune_super_cache operation involving a view_*.php file, but I couldn’t find an explicit entry indicating that the entire cache had been cleared.

My questions are:

  1. Is it normal for WP Super Cache to clear its entire cache when another WordPress plugin is activated, deactivated or updated?
  2. Are there any known WordPress hooks or WP Super Cache mechanisms that could trigger such a purge?
  3. Could another plugin indirectly trigger a full-cache deletion?
  4. Is there a way to prevent these unexpected purges while keeping the preload feature enabled?

I would really appreciate any guidance on identifying the exact cause and preventing this behavior.
I can provide the complete debugging log if needed.
Thank you for your help!

item.title: WP Super Cache needs clearer warnings when caching isn’t working
item.dc:creator: THRIVE - Web Design Gold Coast
item.description:
Replies: 1

Hi team,

We manage a large number of WordPress sites and regularly come across sites where WP Super Cache is installed and active, but caching is either disabled or not working due to configuration errors.

The main issue is that this is far too easy for users to miss.

A few things that would make a big difference:

  • Show a clear dashboard/admin warning when caching is disabled or there is a configuration error.
  • Add a quick link to the WP Super Cache settings from the Plugins page/admin bar.
  • If caching is off, the admin bar should not continue to show “Delete Cache” as though caching is active.
  • Make the current cache status much more obvious throughout the WordPress admin.

We check whether caching is actually working using other methods, and we come across a surprising number of WP Super Cache sites where caching is broken without the site owner realising it.

It would be great if the plugin made this much harder to overlook.

item.title: Still unresolved. Solid Security removing WP_CACHE and breaking WP Super Cache
item.dc:creator: THRIVE - Web Design Gold Coast
item.description:
Replies: 1

Bumping this as the issue is still occurring.

We have just had to manually fix this across hundreds of sites.

Solid Security (formerly iThemes Security) rewrites wp-config.php and removes or relocates the WP_CACHE constant. This causes WP Super Cache to repeatedly report broken caching and recreate advanced-cache.php.

The only reliable fix has been to move WP_CACHE and WPCACHEHOME outside any plugin managed block and place them just above wp-settings.php.

Related threads:
https://wordpress.org/support/topic/conflict-with-wp-super-cache-22/
https://wordpress.org/support/topic/issues-with-solid-security-formerly-ithemes-security-pro/
https://github.com/Automattic/jetpack/issues/25461

Still affecting live production sites.

item.title: Some functionalities breaks when active
item.dc:creator: willpardo
item.description:
Replies: 3

I’ve spent many hours over multiple days using WP Super Cache and trying to resolve a persistent issue on my WordPress + WooCommerce site where the front-end becomes unstable specifically when any page caching is enabled for anonymous/incognito visitors, and I’m at the point where I need a developer-level diagnosis of the root cause. Without caching, everything behaves normally. With caching enabled, the site intermittently renders UI in an incorrect state and various elements break or duplicate, and the behavior is hard to stabilize even after repeated cache purges.

The most visible symptom is that the theme’s off-canvas/mobile panel (the drawer that is normally only used for mobile navigation) sometimes appears open/visible on desktop for logged-out/incognito visitors. When this happens, the panel shows the same mobile navigation content that should only appear after tapping the hamburger icon on mobile. This “panel-open” state can persist while navigating between pages, and sometimes it gradually “self-corrects” after multiple reloads, but it’s not consistent. Importantly, this problem happens primarily for anonymous/incognito visitors; when I’m logged into wp-admin, the issue often does not appear, which strongly suggests a caching-related difference in script execution order, asset delivery, or initial state.

At the same time, other front-end components become unreliable when caching is enabled: category grids shift/corrupt, category pages sometimes lose their filter UI entirely, and in other cases the filter or grid UI appears to be duplicated or re-initialized multiple times while navigating. It feels like JavaScript-based components are being initialized twice (or being initialized on partially styled markup), leading to layout drift, missing elements, or duplicated UI. These issues tend to appear more frequently after moving across multiple category pages and then back/forward, again primarily in incognito/anonymous mode.

I have tested multiple caching approaches and the same pattern persists whenever anonymous page caching is active. I tried the host’s built-in caching controls, then Cache Enabler, then W3 Total Cache, and then WP Super Cache. With W3 Total Cache, enabling Minify/Combine (JS/CSS) made the UI corruption worse, so I disabled Minify and any lazy/delay/defer features and kept only basic page cache + browser cache. With WP Super Cache, I enabled caching for anonymous visitors, disabled caching for logged-in users, set rejected URLs for WooCommerce-sensitive pages (cart/checkout/account), and configured it to avoid caching URLs with GET parameters. Even with conservative settings, the “off-canvas visible on desktop” and “filter/grid corruption” symptoms still occur as soon as caching is enabled.

I also previously changed WooCommerce settings that seemed to affect caching behavior (notably disabling WooCommerce’s order attribution/source tracking feature that sets attribution cookies), and I repeatedly purged caches and flushed permalinks. Additionally, some of the functionality that often misbehaves (especially parts of the header/menu behavior and some UI behavior) is implemented using Code Snippets (custom snippets injected into the site rather than coming directly from the theme or a single plugin), which may be contributing to inconsistent initialization depending on whether the request is cached or not.

I want to be clear that I’m looking for a complete and technically correct solution to make the site compatible with page caching. Suggestions like “just don’t cache the homepage” or “don’t cache category pages” are not acceptable as a real fix, because those are some of the most important pages for performance and SEO; disabling caching there would defeat the purpose and significantly impact site speed. I need to understand why the site behaves differently under cached anonymous responses.

Right now, the current failure mode is primarily on mobile: the intended mobile navigation (provided by Superfly Menu) does not load/activate, and instead the site falls back to the theme’s mobile menu, and additionally the category filter (coming from a separate plugin) does not appear on mobile. If I change configuration to try to force the “correct” Superfly Menu behavior to appear on mobile, the issue flips to the other side: the desktop experience becomes unstable again, with Superfly Menu content appearing on the left as if it were in mobile mode and sometimes looking like it is always open. This “trade-off” strongly suggests a state/initialization problem (possibly related to cached HTML vs. deferred assets, conditional loading of scripts by device detection, or JS executing twice or out of order).
